title: responses-beta: deterministic-seed + metadata passthrough + streaming reassembly handshake
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Add compatibility shim for the new OpenAI 'responses-beta' shape that introduces a top-level deterministicSeed flag and persistent metadata passthrough while improving streaming chunk reassembly for tool/function call boundaries. This PR implements a lightweight proxy layer that maps responses-beta fields into Redwood's internal Responses V2 event stream, preserves seed hints for deterministic modes, and upgrades the streaming assembler to respect seed boundaries and function/toolcall handshake markers. Changes include: 1) API adapter that accepts responses-beta payloads and normalizes 'deterministicSeed' into the internal rngHint metadata and sets a persist_metadata flag when requested; 2) streaming assembler update to buffer and reassemble fragments across network boundaries while ensuring toolcall JSON is emitted atomically; 3) a non-invasive handshake on tool/function calls to surface tool metadata back to callers and downstream observability; 4) tests and end-to-end e2e harness changes to validate determinism across warm/cold KV cache scenarios; 5) docs + examples for SDKs showing how to enable deterministicSeed and metadata persistence. Checklist: - [x] Adapter + translation layer implemented - [x] Streaming reassembler respects seed boundaries - [x] Handshake implemented for toolcalls - [x] Unit + e2e tests added - [x] SDK examples updated - [x] Observability counters and tracing tags added

Notes on backward compatibility: The adapter accepts both legacy OpenAI-style and responses-beta payloads; if deterministicSeed is absent we preserve existing behavior. Metadata passthrough is opt-in to avoid inadvertent data leakage. Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated staging region for 48h, enable gradual rollout with feature flag, monitor reroll metrics (response divergence, latency p50/p95), and provide immediate rollback hook to disable the adapter.
commits: add responses-beta adapter and translation layer
tests: e2e determinism harness and SDK example updates
review_comments: Connor Liu: Left a few inline comments on the assembler regarding backpressure under heavy small-chunk workloads; suggested an opt-in max-buffer-size config.
Maya Patel: Questioned the security implications of metadata passthrough; requested an explicit opt-in config and KMS validation for sensitive metadata keys.
Ethan Novak: Ran performance microbenchmarks and asked for numbers in PR description; requested follow-up to quantify latency impact of seed annotations.

Ava Martinez: Responded that max-buffer-size is configurable with sane defaults (64KB) and added feature flag 'responses_beta_adapter.enabled'. For metadata, explicit allowlist is enforced and documented; KMS validation was added for persisted keys. Performance impact is ~+2ms p50 and +6ms p95 on small-message workloads; added benchmarks to CI_artifacts.zip.
Maya Patel: Approved after allowlist and docs were added. Connor approved after buffer config was exposed. Ethan approved after microbenchmark artifacts uploaded.
merge_commit_message: responses-beta compatibility: add deterministicSeed passthrough, seed-aware streaming assembler, and metadata handshake (ENG-4217)
release_notes: Added compatibility for OpenAI 'responses-beta' including deterministicSeed passthrough and opt-in metadata persistence. Streaming assembler improved to emit atomic tool/function call events and preserve determinism hints. Feature is behind a feature flag 'responses_beta_adapter.enabled' and governed by an allowlist for persisted metadata.
post_merge_actions: Enable canary in staging cluster via rollout script
Create dashboard for responses-beta divergence and seed-violation alerts
Coordinate SDK releases to document deterministicSeed usage
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the adapter minimal and does not change storage schema. Any persistence of metadata is controlled by the allowlist and feature flag. If downstream customers enable persisted metadata, operator must confirm compliance with their data policies.
